She had significant discomfort associated with itchiness and burning sensation. No vesicular rash or acral lesions were noted.

report.source_text: Treatment for the rash included oral antihistamines with loratadine 10 mg daily along with topical triamcinolone 0.1% cream, given the intensity of pruritus. Antiviral therapy with remdesivir was initiated at 200 mg intravenous on day 1, followed by 100 mg intravenous once daily for four more days given her hypoxia.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Severe urticarial rash as the initial symptom of COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath for 1 day and a worsening diffuse urticarial rash over 3 days. On admission, her oxygen saturation was 84% on room air requiring 2 L nasal cannula oxygen. Physical examination showed a widespread erythematous, raised, and pruritic urticarial rash on bilateral upper and lower extremities and the trunk, sparing palms, soles, and mucosa, with intense itching and burning. A COVID-19 test was positive. Chest radiograph revealed left basal atelectasis without major COVID-19 pneumonia. No new medication use or environmental exposures were identified to explain the rash. Treatment with oral loratadine, topical triamcinolone cream, and intravenous remdesivir was initiated. Within 48 hours, there was complete resolution of the rash, supporting the diagnosis of severe urticarial rash as the initial manifestation of COVID-19 infection in this patient with hypoxia and associated shortness of breath.
